messages:
Maya: Noticed repeated hotstart stalls when GPUs fetch layers that are both compressed and sharded. Thinking of adding a per-shard 'staleness_tolerance' hint so loaders can prefer slightly older but local shards over fresh remote ones to avoid tail latency.
Ravi: Interesting. What value range do you imagine? Seconds? Minutes?
Maya: Start with seconds (0-30). If staleness_tolerance>0 loader can accept an earlier manifest version if it's available locally.
Tess: That helps with cold storms but complicates consistency guarantees. We must clearly document that staleness is only allowed for read-only inference models and never for retraining.
Owen: Implementation: loader should check local cache for any manifest snapshot <= staleness_tolerance and validate checksums. If checksums match the older manifest's shards, proceed. Emit metric shard.hotstart.stale_served=true.
Maya: Also add a 'max_stale_age' global per-deployment override so Hosted can opt-out.
ops-bot: INF-5099 created: "staleness_tolerance manifest hint + metrics". Will emit shard.hotstart.stale_served.count and config flag infra.staleness.max_allowed.
Ravi: We should include a brief telemetry experiment: compare p50/p95 latency with staleness off vs 5s vs 20s under pod restart storms. I'll run it on the sim.
Tess: Agreed, and add a warning in the manifest schema that enabling staleness may surface subtle model drift for stateful setups.
Maya: Thanks team, I'll add the manifest field sketch and a short README blurb.
